sudo.notes: From within less, the ! command runs an external shell command, inheriting sudo's elevated privileges.
more supports shell escape via the ! command. Requires the input to be longer than a screen (or use TERM=dumb).
man uses a pager (typically less) that supports shell escape via ! command.

suid.notes: cp with SUID can overwrite arbitrary files; reading from /dev/stdin allows planting a new privileged user in /etc/passwd.
mv with SUID can overwrite arbitrary files; combined with a crafted /etc/passwd entry this yields root.
tee with SUID allows writing to arbitrary root-owned files; planting a sudoers drop-in grants passwordless root.
tar's --checkpoint-action option runs an arbitrary command on each checkpoint; SUID tar yields a root shell.
zip's -T flag invokes the unzip-command to verify the archive; arbitrary commands run with SUID privileges.

sudo.notes: git pages help output through less by default; the pager supports shell escape via ! when running as root.
strace executes the traced program (here /bin/bash) with sudo's elevated privileges.

suid.notes: env executes arbitrary commands; combined with SUID and -p on the shell, preserves privileges.

sudo.notes: env executes /bin/sh as root when invoked through sudo.

suid.notes: dd with SUID can read privileged files (e.g., /etc/shadow) byte-by-byte, enabling offline credential cracking.

sudo.notes: Set the SUID bit on bash, then invoke with -p to preserve privileges and obtain a root shell.
Change ownership of /etc/shadow to the current user, then read or modify password hashes directly.

suid.notes: socat spawns a PTY connected to /bin/sh; with SUID this preserves elevated privileges.

sudo.notes: OpenBSD netcat's -e flag runs a program after connection; here it pushes /bin/sh as root to a listener.
Same as nc — spawn a reverse shell with elevated privileges.
wget can write arbitrary content to root-owned paths; planting a cron job under /etc/cron.d achieves persistent root code execution.
Same as wget — fetch an attacker-controlled cron job and drop it into /etc/cron.d.

suid.notes: Lua's os.execute spawns /bin/sh; combined with SUID yields a root shell.
Node's child_process.spawn invokes /bin/sh with -p to preserve SUID privileges.
PHP's pcntl_exec replaces the current process with /bin/sh -p; preserves SUID privileges.
gdb's embedded Python interpreter can call execl to spawn a privilege-preserving shell.

sudo.notes: Bind-mount /bin/sh over a binary sudo allows the user to run, then re-invoke that binary as root.

commands: sudo docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
sudo.notes: Members of the docker group (or sudo for docker) can mount the host root inside a container and chroot to obtain a root shell.

suid.notes: rsync's -e option specifies the remote shell; pointing it at sh -p preserves SUID privileges.
expect's spawn launches sh with -p to preserve privileges; interact attaches stdio.

sudo.notes: ionice executes an arbitrary command after setting IO scheduling; root shell when run via sudo.
taskset runs a command with a specified CPU affinity; passing /bin/sh yields a root shell.
flock executes a command while holding a file lock; with sudo, the command runs as root.
nice runs a command with adjusted scheduling priority; passing /bin/sh under sudo yields a root shell.
timeout runs a command with a time limit; passing /bin/sh under sudo yields a root shell.
watch's -x flag runs the command without going through sh -c; combined with sudo yields a root shell.
ed supports shell escape via the ! command; spawns a root shell when ed is invoked through sudo.
nano's Read File (^R) followed by Execute Command (^X) runs an arbitrary shell command as root.
